why: a row is a keymap entry: the action, the combination in words, and the chips the view draws — modifiers first, the key last
a system row wears no chip — 'System' on every row is furniture
Enter copies the combination hyprland.lua wants, and the action list is the three copies in order
the view groups by modifier family — Super plus a letter is one keyboard, Super Shift another
the launcher's own keys are listed too — and say when the system owns the same combination, because then the key may never arrive
nothing is deduped: the system bind that owns Ctrl K follows its Oxy namesake — same family, same key, the action's name breaks the tie
CTRL SHIFT and SHIFT CTRL are one family, not two — the canonical order is modifier-weight, whatever the source printed
the bare keys close the keymap — the family nobody modified is the last group
a query narrows by key or by action: 'super' is a word in the family rows, 'f' the key's own word
win is the name people type for Super — the alias finds the family no source calls win
enter is a name no source prints — keyaliases are what make it findable
the plus is punctuation, not a word — 'ctrl+n' is 'ctrl' and 'n', and 'n' leads 'ninth' as well as the N key
a key nobody bound is silence, not an error row
